# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Fill cells with numbers according to constraints*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 block
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicates in rows/columns by blackening cells

### 1.2 Region-Based Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks matching their size
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1–N; duplicates must be separated by their value
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1–N; arrows indicate which neighbor holds the maximum

### 1.3 Cross-Reference / Crossword Style
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells using a provided list of numbers (crossword-style)

---

## 2. REGION DIVISION PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Partition the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

### 2.1 Division into Uniform Shapes
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes (blocks of exactly 5 cells)
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends

### 2.2 Division into Matched Pairs
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a mirror/rotation-matched pair of white and gray cells
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks

### 2.3 Division with Growth/Sequence Constraints
- **Evolomino** — Blocks grow sequentially along arrow paths, each adding one cell to the previous shape

### 2.4 Division with Connectivity and Coloring
- **Choco Banana** — Black rectangles and white irregular regions; numbers indicate region sizes
- **LITS** — Place one tetromino per region; all tetrominoes connect; no 2×2 squares; same-shaped tetrominoes don't touch

---

## 3. CELL SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 3.1 Shading with Adjacency Constraints
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells in rooms per count; no two shaded cells touch; white cells stay connected
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected wall; white islands match given numbers
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells; numbered white cells count visible white cells in four directions
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; each bold-line region contains exactly one wrong number clue
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; circled numbers indicate sum of connected black cell groups

### 3.2 Shading with Structural Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** *(also 2.4)* — Black regions must be rectangles; white regions must not be rectangles
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill exactly the bottom half
- **Norinori** — Shade cells in dominoes; each bold-line region contains exactly two shaded cells

### 3.3 Shading with Path/Maze Constraints
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create a maze; circles lie on shortest path; triangles do not

### 3.4 Shading with Directional/Visibility Constraints
- **Tilepaint** — Shade entire tiles; diagonal-number clues count black cells rightward/downward in their line

### 3.5 Shading with Promontory Constraints
- **Nurimisaki** — Circled cells are promontories (exactly one white neighbor); numbers indicate white-cell run length

---

## 4. LOOP DRAWING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Draw a single closed loop through the grid*

### 4.1 Loops with Circle/Marker Constraints
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; white circles go straight with a turn nearby; black circles turn with straight segments on both sides
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through all black circles, with each circle as the midpoint of a straight segment
- **Slitherlink** — Connect dots to form a loop; numbers indicate how many sides of that cell are used

### 4.2 Loops with Regional Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each room once; alternates between visiting all moons or all suns per room
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold region, loop either turns at all circles or goes straight through all circles; avoids black circles

### 4.3 Loops with Directional / Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Directed loop; black arrow cells set wind direction; loop cannot move against wind; side wind forces a turn
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" exactly once; gate-end numbers indicate crossing order

### 4.4 Loops with Black Cell Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered arrow cells; arrow numbers count black cells in their direction

---

## 5. PATH & CONNECTION PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Draw paths or connections between elements*

### 5.1 Island Bridge Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1–2 per pair); all islands form one connected network

### 5.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping paths that fill the grid

### 5.3 Sequential Path Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snake segments (1–5) in white cells; snakes don't touch; directional visibility constraints apply

---

## 6. OBJECT PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Place specific objects (lights, blocks, symbols) in the grid*

### 6.1 Light/Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

### 6.2 Symbol/Mark Filling
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers indicate the surplus of one symbol; runs constrained by direction

### 6.3 Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** — Place right-triangle halves in cells; remaining white areas must form rectangles; numbers count adjacent triangles

### 6.4 Block/Domino Placement
- **Chained Block** — Fill cells to form numbered blocks; blocks touch only at corners (chains); no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

---

## 7. MOVEMENT & MIGRATION PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Move or route objects from their starting positions*

### 7.1 Circle/Token Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home regions; numbered circles move exact distances; paths don't cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas via straight arrows; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles

### 7.2 Pencil/Line Routing from Fixed Objects
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from their tips; line length matches number in pencil body

---

## 8. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC PUZZLES
*Puzzles combining two or more primary mechanics in roughly equal measure*

| Puzzle | Primary Mechanics Combined |
|---|---|
| **Evolomino** | Region division + sequential shape growth |
| **Sto-stone** | Cell shading + gravity/dropping simulation |
| **Nurimeizu** | Cell shading + shortest-path maze solving |
| **Nuritwin** | Cell shading + region division into matched pairs |
| **Makaro** | Number placement + directional arrow constraints |
| **Ripple Effect** | Number placement + spacing constraints |
| **Sashigane** | Region division + directional arrow routing |
| **Double Choco** | Region division + shape-matching (color symmetry) |

---

## Summary Tree

```
Grid-Based Logic Puzzles
├── 1. Number Placement
│   ├── 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness → Sudoku, Hitori
│   ├── 1.2 Region-Based Filling → Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro
│   └── 1.3 Cross-Reference Style → Nansuke
├── 2. Region Division
│   ├── 2.1 Uniform Shapes → Shikaku, Five Cells, Sashigane
│   ├── 2.2 Matched Pairs → Double Choco, Nuritwin
│   ├── 2.3 Growth/Sequence → Evolomino
│   └── 2.4 Connectivity & Coloring → Choco Banana, LITS
├── 3. Cell Shading
│   ├── 3.1 Adjacency Constraints → Heyawake, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Usowan, Kurotto
│   ├── 3.2 Structural Shape → Choco Banana, Sto-stone, Norinori
│   ├── 3.3 Path/Maze → Nurimeizu
│   ├── 3.4 Directional Clues → Tilepaint
│   └── 3.5 Promontory → Nurimisaki
├── 4. Loop Drawing
│   ├── 4.1 Circle/Marker → Masyu, Mid-loop, Slitherlink
│   ├── 4.2 Regional → Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop
│   ├── 4.3 Directional/Wind → Nagareru, Suraromu
│   └── 4.4 Black Cell → Yajilin
├── 5. Path & Connection
│   ├── 5.1 Island Bridges → Hashiwokakero
│   ├── 5.2 Pair Connection → Numberlink
│   └── 5.3 Sequential Path → Hebi
├── 6. Object Placement
│   ├── 6.1 Illumination → Akari
│   ├── 6.2 Symbol Filling → Juosan
│   ├── 6.3 Triangle Placement → Shakashaka
│   └── 6.4 Block Placement → Chained Block
└── 7. Movement & Migration
    ├── 7.1 Circle/Token → Satogaeri, Yosenabe
    └── 7.2 Pencil Routing → Pencils
```
